ai.description: *Megophrys awuh* is a small frog (30–35 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark, triangular markings. It features prominent, fleshy "horns" above the eyes and a distinct, dark post-orbital streak.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys awuh* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like tubercle on each upper eyelid, which is significantly more prominent than in other Indian *Megophrys* species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys awuh* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Naga Hills, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Naga Hills horned frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush passing insects while avoiding detection by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys awuh* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys awuh* is endemic to the high-altitude forests of Nagaland in Northeast India, specifically occurring at elevations between 1,800 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Naga Hills Horned Frog emits a series of short, metallic "clinking" notes, typically heard emanating from leaf litter near fast-flowing streams in montane forests.
